text: IMF Pledges Support as Iraq Seeks Emergency Financial Assistance Iraq has approached the International Monetary Fund (IMF) for a new financial program as the US-Israel war with Iran disrupts oil exports and squeezes government revenue. IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva pledged “firm” support, including financing and policy assistance, though the size and terms of the program remain undecided. The IMF forecasts Iraq’s economy will contract 16% in 2026 before rebounding 19% in 2027. The crisis has also prompted Iraq to devalue its currency by 13% against the dollar as disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz hit oil shipments. The IMF is simultaneously advancing discussions on potential support for Lebanon, highlighting mounting economic pressures across the Middle East.

text: European Gas Prices Surge to Highest Level Since 2022 Amid Middle East Risks European natural gas prices climbed to their highest level since December 2022 as renewed security concerns in the Middle East threatened global energy supplies. Reports of an attack on a liquefied natural gas (LNG) tanker near Yemen heightened fears of further disruptions to shipments, particularly through critical Middle Eastern shipping routes. Benchmark Dutch gas futures rose as much as 2%, extending the previous week’s rally as traders assessed the risk of tighter supplies ahead of winter. Europe’s energy outlook remains vulnerable due to low gas inventories, which are just over 74% full compared with the five-year seasonal average of 89%. Although mild weather has supported storage refilling, prolonged supply disruptions and rising winter demand could push prices higher. European gas prices have already more than doubled from pre-conflict levels, increasing pressure on businesses, consumers and the wider economy. Analysts warn that prices could rise further if Middle Eastern LNG exports remain constrained and competition for global gas supplies intensifies.

text: US Stocks Rebound as Investors Await Big Tech Earnings US stock futures rebounded after a sharp selloff in chip stocks, offering relief to investors at the start of a crucial week for technology earnings. Nasdaq 100 futures rose 1.3%, while S&P 500 futures gained 0.7%, as investors looked ahead to results from Meta Platforms, Tesla and major semiconductor companies. The earnings reports are expected to provide important clues about the strength of the artificial intelligence (AI) trade and whether heavy investment in AI infrastructure can generate sufficient returns. Despite the recovery, financial markets remain volatile amid uncertainty over inflation, interest rates and upcoming US midterm elections. Investors are also monitoring developments in Europe, where French political unrest has increased pressure on government bonds and weakened the euro. Meanwhile, Brent crude prices fell to around $107 a barrel, while gold edged higher. Market sentiment will likely depend on corporate earnings, central bank expectations and whether technology stocks can regain investor confidence.

text: France’s Bond Market Falls as Riots Intensify Pressure on Government France’s government bond prices fell as violent protests over the rising cost of living intensified across the country. The unrest increased concerns among investors about political instability and the government’s ability to manage the country’s growing debt and budget deficit. The gap between French and German 10-year bond yields widened to 146 basis points, while the euro weakened and France’s CAC 40 stock index dropped 1.2%. The protests have created a difficult challenge for the government as it tries to control public anger while reducing the budget deficit. The proposed 2027 budget includes €43 billion in measures to improve public finances, but political divisions could make an agreement difficult. Continued unrest and uncertainty surrounding the upcoming presidential election may further weaken investor confidence and increase pressure on French financial markets.
